target_customer: Consumers organizing social events and groups; a live video angle was floated in 2007
problem: Group event planning and coordination, and possibly live video sharing. Sources are thin and not consistent.

founders.name: Russ d'Sa
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Russell d'Sa and his current bio as founder and CEO of LiveKit; no earlier employer or school found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Event planning and RSVP tools were standard web engineering in 2007; a live video product would be harder but nothing shows it shipped.

defensibility.rationale: Social planning tools were easily copied and had no data or network advantage at launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found; no source describes an incumbent response.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand for Meetyu was found; group event planning and live video were both crowded consumer categories as Facebook and MySpace grew in 2007.

branding.domain_note: meetyu.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page (checked 2026).

identity.logo: YC page shows a placeholder logo

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found; many similarly spelled names (MeetYou, Meetyoo) exist.

outcome_analysis: Meetyu was a Summer 2007 YC company run by one named founder and is now inactive. A 2007 Hacker News post described a stealth live video product planning a September launch and seeking a cofounder, while Crunchbase describes event planning. The cause of the shutdown is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: Product description conflicts: Crunchbase says event planning, a Hacker News post dated 2007-08-21 suggests live video (both seen only as search snippets). Funding search returned only similarly named companies. No competitor source dated near the batch connects to Meetyu, so the list is empty. Website is a parked domain. Shutdown cause not found.
